subject: Proposal: Salary Spectrum Update & Approval Flow
body:
From: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>
To: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
Cc: Sara Park <sara@compbench.com>
Date: Mon, 15 Mar 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Proposal: Salary Spectrum Update & Approval Flow

Team —

Attaching a fresh draft of the salary spectrum (2027Q2_salary_spectrum_v2.xlsx) and our external market write-up from CompBench. The ask:

- Replace the current fixed-band anchors with a continuous "spectrum" approach that reduces cliff effects between L3-L6.
- Update geo multipliers for US/EMEA/APAC; CompBench has provided percentile curves by market (see attached PDF).
- Define a simple approval flow for: (a) level-to-salary adjustments at offer, (b) exceptions (>20% off-band), and (c) localized market uplifts for critical hires.

Key constraints: headcount is flat this quarter; changes must not materially increase run-rate >2% without exec sign-off. I propose the following approval thresholds: up to 10% off-band = hiring manager + HR sign-off; 10-20% = HR + Finance; >20% = Compensation Committee + CFO.

Please review the spectrum sheet (tabs: US_base, EMEA_adj, APAC_adj, mapping_rules) and the CompBench summary. Sara — could you confirm the 50/90 percentile anchors you used and whether the APAC panel included on-contract hires?

Thanks,
Mina Haddad
Head of Talent Strategy
Redwood Inference

Attachments: 2027Q2_salary_spectrum_v2.xlsx

---

From: Sara Park <sara@compbench.com>
To: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 15 Mar 2027 13:34:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Proposal: Salary Spectrum Update & Approval Flow

Mina / team —

Thanks for sharing. Quick summary from our end (attached: comp-bench-market-report-2027.pdf):

- We modeled base salary percentiles for each role family using aggregated market comp data (50th, 75th, 90th). For L3-L6 engineering cohorts the biggest delta is in West Coast tech hubs (SF/SEA) vs midsized US markets.
- Recommendation: spectrum anchors at 30th/60th/90th instead of 25th/50th/75th; this smooths offer steps and keeps mid-market competitiveness while protecting runway.
- APAC panel: included a mix of on-payroll and contractor-adjusted equivalents; we applied a 0.78 conversion factor to normalize contractor comp into full-time-equivalent base.

Notes on exceptions: we usually see exceptions concentrated in senior IC / staff+ where scarcity premium applies. For those, the governance you propose seems reasonable.

I can update the pdf to include a simple mapping table (role -> suggested anchor percentiles) if that helps.

—Sara
Sara Park
Principal Analyst, CompBench
sara@compbench.com

Attachment: comp-bench-market-report-2027.pdf

---

From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
To: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>, Sara Park <sara@compbench.com>
Date: Tue, 16 Mar 2027 10:08:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Proposal: Salary Spectrum Update & Approval Flow

Mina —

This looks thorough. A couple of practical points from People Ops:

1) Level mapping: please include a clear mapping table for L4/L5 engineering -> equivalent non-engineering titles. We've had confusion in offers when hiring managers pick the wrong band.
2) Localized pay letters: if we change to spectrum anchors, offer templates need a brief paragraph explaining what the spectrum is and why candidates may land anywhere within it. Legal will want consistent language across regions.
3) Pilot: recommend we run this spectrum for all offers to the sales hiring cohort (10 hires) and 20% of engineering offers over the next 6 weeks before full rollout. That will limit churn and let us validate acceptance rates.

I'll flag two compliance items separately to legal (data retention on market inputs; record of exceptions).

Laura Bennett
Head of People Operations
Redwood Inference

---

From: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>
To: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 17 Mar 2027 08:21:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Proposal: Salary Spectrum Update & Approval Flow

Agree with the thresholds and pilot approach. A few finance considerations:

- 2% run-rate tolerance is OK, but we need line-level visibility by headcount bucket for the next two quarters. Can you include an estimated delta P&L tab in the XLS with candidate-velocity scenarios?
- For exceptions >10% we should require Finance sign-off with a short economic rationale (comp-to-budget delta + expected time-to-hire benefit).
- Compensation Committee involvement for >20% exceptions should include a recommended fallback model (e.g., offers with phased increases tied to 6-month performance milestones) to reduce upfront hit.

If HR/People Ops and Legal are comfortable, I'm fine with moving this to a formal HR policy doc and routing to Exec for sign-off next Tuesday.

Aditya Rao
VP, Finance
Redwood Inference

---

From: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>
To: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
Cc: Sara Park <sara@compbench.com>
Date: Wed, 17 Mar 2027 16:44:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Proposal: Salary Spectrum Update & Approval Flow

Thanks all — summary and next steps below. Pulling this thread into HR-221 (Jira) and uploading updated assets to the Drive folder.

Decisions made:
- Adopt spectrum anchors at 30/60/90 for initial pilot.
- Approval thresholds confirmed: <=10% (Mgr + HR); 10-20% (HR + Finance); >20% (Comp Committee + CFO).
- Pilot cohort: Sales hires (all offers) + 20% of engineering offers for 6 weeks.

Action items (owners):
- Mina: update XLS with P&L delta scenarios and candidate-velocity tabs; upload by Fri 19 Mar. (Attachment: 2027Q2_salary_spectrum_v2.xlsx)
- Sara / CompBench: provide role->anchor mapping table by Thu 18 Mar and confirm APAC contractor normalization details.
- Laura: draft offer-language paragraph and pilot SOP; coordinate with Legal. Due Mon 22 Mar.
- Aditya: prepare Comp Committee slate and fallback offer templates for >20% exceptions; coordinate CFO availability for Exec sign-off.
- Neha: maintain exception log and ensure records for compliance.

Links: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/HR-221; https://drive.redwood.com/drive/folders/offer-framework

I'll queue Exec review for Tue 23 Mar assuming docs are ready. If anything blocks that timeline, call it out in Jira.

Best,
Mina
Head of Talent Strategy
Redwood Inference

Attachments referenced: 2027Q2_salary_spectrum_v2.xlsx, comp-bench-market-report-2027.pdf
